answer: Trust propagates through bounded random walks on the attestation graph, so voting influence depends on reachable, mutually supported attestations rather than identities alone. A sybil cluster with few links to honest participants has a sparse external cut and low conductance; spectral mixing limits how much trust crosses that boundary, while min-cut transitivity bounds aggregate voting weight. Even when lotus, delta, and river are adversarial labels, they gain no weight merely by multiplying identities.
